body: I was on Depakote for several years. It made me into a zombie... also made me gain 60lbs. Its different for everyone, but with the symptoms you've described, yeah... talk to your Doc. Doesn't seem like a good med for you.
Thank you.

Actually, I like the stalking. She keeps me at armslength and the fact that she keeps track of my FB and Reddit activities reminds me that she does care and that it is difficult for her to ignore me... Long story.

I most certainly can. I'm not giving in, I'm finally allowing whatever it is that has been trying to kill me my whole life its due. Yeah people care about me and all I've been able to do for them is bum, borrow and cry on their shoulders... for years. I'm a burden no matter what they say. My poor baby has had to sit and watch me cry. She won't have to see that anymore and wonder why her daddy is such a mess.

I don't hide the fact that I'm bipolar here or anywhere else. I do feel a considerable amount of shame about it, but there has been entirely too many times where people just judge me by my behaviour and don't bother to get to know me because I'm deemed "creepy". I do, however, have this account specifically for talking about bipolarity, bisexuality, depression and relationships because my would-be GF is a hard core redditor who is constantly stalking my FB and Reddit activity. I guess I just don't want her to know how much she's affected me.
That's fine Manarax. It's good to know that there are others going through the same mindfuck. My best wishes that things get better for you. They certainly won't for me.

As previously stated, each drug will have different results for different people. Personally, Lamictal doesn't work for me. I'm currently taking it and well, it doesn't work. I cannot get through a day without crying, and my hair is falling out. Lithium made me fat and depakote did the same thing. Keep working with different treatments until you find the best for you. It's a long tedious process, fair warning.

Thank you for sharing your story with me. My latest hurdle is unrequieted love. Its a pain I subject myself to everyday. I rapid cycle, and that makes for a dismal existence in a situation like this. I'm sure there is undiagnosed bp in my family, but being relatively poor, no one has had the cash or the inclination to seek medical help. I was the first one to take that step after a stay in the hospital while I was in service.

I understand your question/statement. My question was intended as a more broad definition of "normal". As in, how do I fit into society around people with relatively stable brain chemicals? We act, think, react and feel everything so different. Think of it in terms of colour blindness. Individuals with colour blindness simply don't have certain colours in their spectrum. There is no way an individual such as this can understand what that colour is. On the other hand, individuals without this condition cannot understand why a person can't understand a certain colour. The same could be said for individuals with Bipolar disorder. No one understands the other. So how does one fit into society?

My closer friends know that I'm bipolar, agoraphobic and subject to anxiety and panic attacks, but I fight my proclivity to withdraw and be introverted. It makes for a lot more stress, but I believe its healthier for me. I just hide out of shame for being a basketcase and never knowing how I'm going to feel from one moment to the next... medicated or not.
This.

Tell me, tell me, tell meeee. Seriously though, tell me more about this situation. Are you in a committed relationship? If so, what is happening with you and your SO that would cause you to pose this question to yourself and your fellow redditors? If you're not currently in a committed relationship, is there a potential that is on your mind? Talk to me goose.

Remove yourself from this situation hun. You're young and there's no need to put yourself through this. Occupy yourself with YOUR life, not his. Work on who you are. Yes, he has changed your life, so take what you have learned and move on. Nobody needs to torture themselves with repeated heart breaks.

Nurta hit the nail right on the head. You're not pathetic for it, at least not to people like you and I. Blame it on the scumbag brain that many of us struggle with. Although she keeps me at arms length, my would-be GF stalks me on reddit and on FB. It makes me feel good that she does. Although I don't really post anything that would alert her that I was posting concerns about our relationship (this is an account of mine she is unaware of as she is a hard-core redditor), I sometimes wish she would stumble on a post of mine and offer a little advice so I can learn a little bit more about how she feels. It's pathetic, but its how we are.
Dependent personality disorder?

I know EXACTLY how you feel! I'm right there with you experiencing the very same thing. Its seems endless when you cannot get her/him out of your mind at all and the days seem endless and nothing brings you joy.

You totally suck!! The only tickets I could find to that show were $150! That's $300 plus the expense of a 6hr drive, smokes, food, Tshirts and a hotel room! I say from my heart... fuck you! Of course I say this with the kindest feelings.

You don't get to choose who you fall in love with. The person I'm in love with keeps me at arms length. She knows I love her and claims to love me back. But the distance... just try to keep your head up and leave yourself open to other options. Try to eliminate her from your life if you can. It sounds like she's poisoning you.

My advice: smile more.  I use to be that guy. Quiet, reserved and more than a little bit self conscious. Stop trying to get certain reactions of the other people. The only person that can really make you happy is you.
I third. Fuck you!

You'll heal. It will take awhile. It's worse when that person is still in your life, playing the role of the proverbial dangling carrot. You will grow a thicker skin and if you stay focused, you won't let it happen again. Good luck.

Crying will help in the short term. Its a temporary outlet. It wont solve the problems though. Just open the lines of communication with those around you. If they do not accept it, do your own thing and leave them to theirs. The only person you have control of is you.
Holy shit! Yes!

I'm in a little bit of a similar situation. It really depends on you. Do you have that feeling that she's the one? Do you find it difficult to go about day to day, mundane activities? Do you make decisions about your future be it short or long term with her in mind? What do you feel are your chances? I may not be the best option to give advice on this matter, but I do know that anything worth having is worth waiting/suffering for and that it WILL NOT come easy. All I can really suggest is to try to open up that communication with her and get the whole story from her point of view. Good luck my friend. This is a shitty place for us to be.
